senses.def: to put something over or on something to hide, protect, or decorate it
examples: Cover the pot and let the rice cook for 15 minutes.
Snow covered the whole town overnight.

senses.def: to include or deal with a subject, or to report on an event
examples: The exam will cover chapters one through five.
She covered the election for a national newspaper.

senses.def: to be enough money to pay for something, or to protect someone with insurance
examples: My salary barely covers the rent.
Does your insurance cover dental care?

senses.def: something that goes over or protects something, or a place that gives shelter
examples: Don't judge a book by its cover.
When the shooting started, everyone ran for cover.

note: "Cover for someone" = do their work while they're away. "Cover up" = hide a mistake or crime.

senses.def: the way news or sports events are reported on TV, radio, or in newspapers
examples: The trial received wide coverage in the national media.
Live coverage of the game starts at seven.

senses.def: the amount of protection an insurance policy gives, or the area a service reaches
examples: Many part-time workers don't have health coverage.
There's no cell phone coverage up in the mountains.

senses.def: having a layer of something on it
examples: The kids came home covered in mud.
The hills were covered with wildflowers.

senses.def: having a roof or cover over it
examples: We waited for the bus in a covered shelter.

senses.def: a large female farm animal kept for milk or meat
examples: The farmer milks the cows twice a day.
A herd of cows was blocking the country road.

note: "Cash cow" = a product that makes steady profit. "Holy cow!" is an informal exclamation of surprise.

senses.def: a thin line on a surface where it has broken but not split apart
examples: There's a long crack in the windshield.
Water was leaking through a crack in the ceiling.

senses.def: to break without separating into pieces, or to break something open
examples: The ice cracked under his weight.
Crack two eggs into a bowl and whisk them.

senses.def: to solve a difficult problem or code, or to lose control under pressure
examples: Police finally cracked the case after six months.
He cracked under the pressure of the final interview.

note: "Crack down on" = deal with something much more strictly. "Crack a joke" = tell a joke.

senses.def: an activity that needs skill in making things by hand
examples: The market sells local crafts like pottery and woven baskets.
Woodworking is a craft that takes years to master.

senses.def: the skills needed for a particular job or art
examples: She spent years perfecting her craft as a writer.

senses.def: to make something carefully and skillfully
examples: Each chair is crafted by hand from solid oak.
The speech was carefully crafted to appeal to young voters.

note: "Craft" can also mean a boat or aircraft; the plural is still "craft". "Crafty" means clever in a dishonest way.

senses.def: an accident in which a vehicle hits something
examples: Three people were injured in a car crash on the highway.
Investigators are still looking into the cause of the plane crash.

senses.def: to hit something violently, or to make a vehicle do this
examples: He crashed his dad's car into a tree.
The helicopter crashed shortly after takeoff.

senses.def: to suddenly stop working, or to suddenly lose a lot of value
examples: My laptop crashed and I lost the whole document.
Stock prices crashed after the bank collapsed.

note: A "crash course" is a short, intensive course. Informally, "crash" can mean sleep somewhere: "Can I crash on your couch?"

senses.def: to move on your hands and knees, or with your body close to the ground
examples: The baby is just starting to crawl.
Soldiers crawled under the barbed wire.

senses.def: (of traffic or time) to move very slowly
examples: Traffic crawled along the freeway for an hour.

senses.def: to be full of people, insects, or other things moving around
examples: The kitchen floor was crawling with ants.

note: "Make your skin crawl" = make you feel disgusted or afraid. As a noun, "crawl" is also a swimming stroke.

senses.def: not sensible; very foolish or strange
examples: It's crazy to drive in this snow without proper tires.
That's the craziest idea I've ever heard.

senses.def: mentally ill (offensive), or very angry or upset
examples: The noise from the construction is driving me crazy.

senses.def: very enthusiastic about or in love with someone or something
examples: My nephew is crazy about dinosaurs.
He's crazy about her.

note: Informal. Using it to mean "mentally ill" can be offensive. "Like crazy" = very much or very fast.

senses.def: the thick fatty part of milk, used in cooking or on desserts
examples: Do you take cream in your coffee?
She served the strawberries with whipped cream.

senses.def: a thick substance you put on your skin
examples: Rub some cream on your hands to stop them from cracking.
The doctor gave me an antibiotic cream for the cut.

senses.def: having a pale yellowish-white color
examples: They painted the living room walls cream.

note: "The cream of the crop" = the best people or things in a group. Americans say "sunscreen" more than "sun cream".

senses.def: to make something new exist or happen
examples: The new factory will create 500 jobs.
Click here to create a new account.

senses.def: to cause a particular situation, feeling, or impression
examples: The delay created a lot of confusion at the airport.
Soft lighting helps create a relaxing atmosphere.

senses.def: the act or process of making something new or causing it to exist
examples: The plan focuses on job creation in rural areas.
Since its creation in 1995, the charity has helped thousands of families.

senses.def: something new that someone has made, especially something original or artistic
examples: The chef's latest creation is a chocolate and chili dessert.

senses.def: the making of the world by God, or the whole world and everything in it
examples: Many cultures have their own stories about the creation of the world.

senses.def: using imagination and skill to produce new ideas or works of art
examples: She's a very creative person who's always making something.
We need some creative solutions to cut costs.

senses.def: connected with producing art, writing, music, or design
examples: He teaches creative writing at the community college.

note: "Creative accounting" is a polite way of saying dishonest bookkeeping.

senses.def: the ability to use imagination and skill to produce new ideas or works of art
examples: The new office layout is designed to encourage creativity.
Strict rules can kill children's creativity.

senses.def: a person who has made, invented, or started something
examples: The show's creator also wrote most of the episodes.
Content creators earn money from ads on their videos.

senses.def: God, as the maker of the world
examples: Many religions believe in one Creator of all things.

senses.def: any living thing that can move, such as an animal, or an imaginary being
examples: The deep ocean is full of strange creatures we know little about.
The movie is about a creature that lives under the lake.

senses.def: a person of a particular type
examples: My grandfather is a creature of habit: same breakfast every day for forty years.

note: "Creature comforts" = things that make life physically comfortable, like good food and a warm bed.

senses.def: the quality that makes people believe or trust someone or something
examples: The scandal badly damaged the senator's credibility.
Citing reliable sources gives your essay more credibility.

senses.def: able to be believed or trusted
examples: Police received a credible threat against the school.
The witness gave a credible account of what happened.

senses.def: good enough to be taken seriously or likely to succeed
examples: She is the only credible candidate running against the mayor.

note: Don't confuse with "credulous" (too ready to believe things). "Incredible" now usually means "amazing".

senses.def: an arrangement to receive goods or money now and pay for them later
examples: They bought the furniture on credit.
Small businesses are struggling to get credit from banks.

senses.def: praise or approval for something good that someone has done
examples: She never gets credit for all the extra work she does.
To his credit, he admitted the mistake right away.

senses.def: a unit that measures a completed part of a college course
examples: You need 120 credits to graduate.

senses.tr: (hesaba) para yatırmak, alacak kaydetmek; (başarıyı) birine atfetmek
senses.def: to add money to a bank account, or to say that someone deserves praise for something
examples: The refund will be credited to your account within five days.
She credits her coach with saving her career.

note: "The credits" are the list of names at the end of a film. "Take credit for" = claim you did something.

senses.def: to move slowly and quietly so that you are not seen or heard
examples: He crept upstairs so he wouldn't wake the baby.
The cat crept toward the bird in the grass.

senses.def: to increase or change slowly, often without being noticed
examples: Prices have been creeping up all year.
A few errors crept into the final report.

senses.def: (informal) an unpleasant person, especially one who makes others feel uncomfortable
examples: Some creep kept staring at her on the train.

note: Irregular verb: creep – crept – crept. "Give someone the creeps" = make them feel uneasy.

senses.def: all the people who work on a ship, plane, or train
examples: The plane had 150 passengers and six crew on board.
The crew abandoned the ship when the fire spread.

senses.def: a group of people who work together on a particular job
examples: A film crew was shooting a scene on our street.
Road crews worked through the night to clear the snow.

note: "Crew" is a group noun; you can say "the crew is" or "the crew are". American English prefers "is".

senses.def: an illegal act, or illegal activities in general
examples: He was arrested for a crime he didn't commit.
Violent crime has fallen in most big cities.

senses.def: something that seems wrong, wasteful, or shameful
examples: It's a crime to throw away all that good food.

note: You "commit" a crime, not "do" or "make" one.

senses.def: a person who has committed a crime
examples: The police caught the criminals at the border.
Many career criminals start offending as teenagers.

senses.def: connected with crime or with the laws dealing with crime
examples: He has no criminal record.
The company is facing a criminal investigation.

senses.def: (informal) morally very wrong or shocking
examples: It's criminal how much they charge for a cup of coffee here.

senses.def: a time of great difficulty or danger when important decisions must be made
examples: The country is in the middle of an economic crisis.
Thousands fled during the refugee crisis.

senses.def: a time of serious personal or emotional difficulty
examples: At 45, he went through a midlife crisis and bought a motorcycle.

note: Plural: crises /ˈkraɪsiːz/.

senses.def: standards used to judge or decide something (plural of criterion)
examples: Applicants must meet strict criteria to receive the scholarship.
What criteria do you use to choose a new employee?

note: Criteria is plural: "these criteria are". The singular is "criterion", though many people wrongly say "a criteria".

senses.def: a standard or principle used to judge something or make a decision
examples: Price was not the only criterion we considered when buying the car.
The main criterion for admission is academic performance.

note: Irregular plural: criterion → criteria.

senses.def: a person whose job is to write opinions about books, films, music, food, etc.
examples: The film was praised by critics but failed at the box office.
She works as a restaurant critic for a city magazine.

senses.def: a person who openly says they disapprove of someone or something
examples: Critics of the plan say it will raise taxes for the middle class.

note: Trap for Turkish speakers: "critic" is a person; "kritik" (criticism, review) is "criticism" or "critique".

senses.def: saying what you think is bad about someone or something
examples: The report was highly critical of the hospital's management.
Why are you always so critical of my friends?

senses.def: extremely important because the result depends on it
examples: The next 48 hours are critical for the investigation.
Clean water is critical to public health.

senses.def: very serious or dangerous, especially in illness
examples: Two victims are in critical condition at the hospital.

senses.def: carefully judging the good and bad qualities of something
examples: The course teaches students critical thinking skills.

note: "Critical acclaim" = praise from critics.

senses.def: in a way that judges carefully or points out faults
examples: Students should learn to read news sources critically.
He spoke critically about the government's response.

senses.tr: ağır şekilde, ciddi biçimde; son derece
senses.def: seriously or dangerously, or extremely
examples: Two people were critically injured in the fire.
It is critically important to finish on time.

senses.def: by critics who review books, films, etc.
examples: The album was critically acclaimed but sold poorly.

senses.def: the act of saying what is wrong with someone or something, or a comment that does this
examples: The new policy has faced strong criticism from teachers.
She doesn't take criticism well.

senses.def: the work of judging and discussing books, art, music, etc.
examples: He studied literary criticism in graduate school.

note: "Constructive criticism" is helpful, meant to improve something.

senses.def: to say what you think is bad or wrong about someone or something
examples: The mayor was criticized for ignoring the housing crisis.
Stop criticizing everything I cook!

note: American spelling with -ize; British also uses "criticise". Pattern: criticize someone FOR something.

senses.def: a careful written or spoken analysis of the good and bad points of something
examples: The book offers a sharp critique of modern consumer culture.
Each student must write a critique of a classmate's essay.

senses.def: to analyze and judge the strengths and weaknesses of something
examples: The teacher critiqued our designs one by one.

note: More formal and academic than "criticism", and not necessarily negative.

senses.def: a plant grown in large amounts, especially for food
examples: Corn and soybeans are the main crops in Iowa.
The drought destroyed most of this year's crop.

senses.def: a group of people or things that appear at the same time
examples: This year's crop of graduates faces a tough job market.

senses.def: to cut off the edges of a picture, or to cut hair very short
examples: Crop the photo so only the two of us are in it.

note: Phrasal verb "crop up" = happen or appear unexpectedly: "Something cropped up at work."

senses.def: to go from one side of something to the other
examples: Look both ways before you cross the street.
Thousands of migrants try to cross the border every month.

senses.def: to come into your mind briefly, or to put one leg or arm over the other
examples: It never crossed my mind that she might be lying.
He sat back and crossed his arms.

senses.def: a mark (X or +), or the symbol of Christianity
examples: Put a cross next to the answers you're not sure about.
She wore a small gold cross around her neck.

senses.def: a mix of two different things, breeds, or types
examples: The dog is a cross between a poodle and a Labrador.

note: "Cross your fingers" = hope for luck. In British English, "cross" can also be an adjective meaning "annoyed".

senses.def: a large number of people gathered together in one place
examples: A crowd of fans waited outside the stadium.
The crowd cheered when the band came on stage.

senses.def: a particular group of people, especially friends with similar interests
examples: He started hanging out with the wrong crowd in high school.

senses.def: to gather together in large numbers, often filling a space
examples: Tourists crowded around the street performer.

senses.def: full of people, often too many
examples: The subway is always crowded during rush hour.
We couldn't find a table in the crowded restaurant.

senses.def: full of competitors or things
examples: The startup is entering a crowded market for food delivery apps.

senses.def: a circle of gold and jewels that a king or queen wears on the head
examples: The queen's crown is kept in a museum in London.
She wore a paper crown at her birthday party.

senses.def: the title of champion in a sports competition
examples: The team is hoping to defend its crown next season.

senses.def: to officially make someone a king or queen, or to make something complete with a final success
examples: She was crowned Miss America in 2019.
Winning the final crowned a perfect season.

note: A "crown" is also a cap a dentist puts on a damaged tooth. "Crowning achievement" = the best thing someone has done.

senses.def: extremely important because it affects what happens next
examples: Getting enough sleep is crucial for good health.
The goalkeeper made a crucial save in the final minute.

senses.def: in a natural state, before being processed
examples: The price of crude oil fell below $70 a barrel.
Crude rubber is treated with chemicals to make tires.

senses.def: simple and not made or done with much skill or detail
examples: The prisoners made a crude knife from a spoon.
This is only a crude estimate of the costs.

senses.def: rude and offensive, especially about sex
examples: He made a crude joke that embarrassed everyone at dinner.

note: In news, "crude" alone often means crude oil: "Crude rose 2% on Monday."

senses.def: wanting to cause pain or suffering to others, or causing great suffering
examples: It's cruel to keep a dog chained up all day.
Losing in the last second was a cruel blow for the team.

note: "You have to be cruel to be kind" = sometimes hurting someone is for their own good.

senses.def: a vacation on a large ship that visits several places
examples: My parents went on a Caribbean cruise for their anniversary.
The cruise stops in five ports along the coast.

senses.def: to travel by ship for pleasure, or to move at a steady comfortable speed
examples: We cruised around the Greek islands for a week.
The plane was cruising at 35,000 feet.

senses.def: to win or succeed easily
examples: The home team cruised to a 5-0 victory.

senses.def: to press something so hard that it breaks or loses its shape
examples: Crush two cloves of garlic and add them to the pan.
His car was crushed by a falling tree.

senses.def: to defeat someone or something completely, often using force
examples: The army crushed the rebellion within days.
We crushed them 42 to 7.

senses.def: to make someone feel extremely sad or disappointed
examples: She was crushed when she didn't get the part.

senses.def: a strong but usually short-lived romantic feeling for someone
examples: I had a huge crush on my English teacher in eighth grade.

note: "Have a crush on someone" is very common, informal, and not serious love.

senses.def: to produce tears because you are sad, hurt, or very emotional
examples: The baby cried all night.
She cried when she read her father's letter.

senses.def: to shout something loudly
examples: "Watch out!" she cried, as the car came toward us.

senses.def: a loud sound expressing a strong feeling, or a shout
examples: We heard a cry for help from the river.
The crowd let out a cry of joy.

note: "A far cry from" = very different from. "Crying shame" = a very sad or unfair situation.

senses.def: a small solid piece of a substance with regular sides, formed naturally
examples: Salt crystals formed on the rocks as the seawater dried.
Snowflakes are made of tiny ice crystals.

senses.def: high-quality clear glass used for fine glasses and decorations
examples: They received a set of crystal wine glasses as a wedding gift.

note: "Crystal clear" = completely clear or easy to understand: "Let me make this crystal clear."

senses.def: an action or event that signals someone to do something
examples: When the music stops, that's your cue to walk on stage.
She took her cue from the host and started eating.

senses.def: a long stick used to hit the ball in pool or billiards
examples: He chalked the end of his cue before taking the shot.

note: "Right on cue" = at exactly the expected moment. Don't confuse with British "queue" (line), which sounds the same.

senses.def: a small religious group with extreme beliefs, often controlled by one leader
examples: Her parents spent years trying to get her out of the cult.

senses.def: a way of life, idea, or person that has become extremely popular
examples: Some critics complain about the cult of celebrity on social media.

senses.def: very popular with a particular group of fans
examples: The movie flopped at first but later became a cult classic.
The band has a cult following in Japan.

senses.def: to prepare land and grow crops on it
examples: Farmers here have cultivated rice for centuries.
Only a small part of the land is suitable for cultivating.

senses.def: to try to develop a quality, skill, or relationship
examples: She has cultivated an image as a tough negotiator.
It's worth cultivating good relationships with your clients.

senses.def: connected with the customs, beliefs, and way of life of a society
examples: Moving abroad can be a big cultural shock.
The city has a rich cultural heritage.

senses.def: connected with art, music, theater, and literature
examples: The festival is the biggest cultural event of the year.

senses.def: the customs, beliefs, art, and way of life of a particular society or group
examples: Food is an important part of Turkish culture.
Children of immigrants often grow up between two cultures.

senses.def: the attitudes and behavior typical of an organization or group
examples: The company has a culture of working late every night.

senses.def: art, music, literature, and similar activities
examples: Paris is full of culture: museums, theaters, and galleries.

note: In Turkish, "kültürlü" (educated) is closer to "cultured" or "well-read" in English.

senses.def: a small container with a handle used for drinking, or the amount it holds
examples: Would you like a cup of coffee?
Add one cup of flour to the mixture.

senses.def: a large metal cup given as a prize, or the competition for it
examples: Brazil has won the World Cup five times.

note: "Not my cup of tea" = not something I like. In US recipes, a "cup" is a standard measure (about 240 ml).
